reason: The text demonstrates Yahweh's protective intervention on behalf of David, a figure destined to lead Israel. Abigail explicitly refers to Yahweh as 'God of Israel' and acknowledges that Yahweh has prevented David from shedding blood and will appoint him as a leader over Israel (וצוך לנגיד על ישראל). Additionally, Yahweh strikes down Nabal, administering justice. These divine actions—preventing bloodshed, positioning righteous leadership, and executing justice—serve to support and protect the Hebrew people through the establishment of just governance.
